query: Use the optical and SAR images together to identify built-up and water-covered regions.
answer: Optical evidence: water-covered regions estimated at 4.2% of the scene. Prominent water bodies are visible. SAR evidence: low-backscatter smooth regions cover ~2.7% — consistent with water (specular, low return). SAR penetrates cloud and operates day/night; water appears dark/smooth due to specular reflection, built-up appears bright due to double-bounce. Water: optical (4.2%) and SAR (2.7%) agree strongly (IoU 0.61); fused high-confidence water 2.6% — SAR corroborates optical water detection (SAR water is dark/smooth, robust to cloud). Built-up: low agreement (IoU 0.00); optical 0.5% vs SAR 1.0% — difference reflects sensor physics (SAR sees structure, optical sees reflectance). Overall cross-modal agreement: moderate agreement (mean IoU 0.30, water Dice 0.76, built Dice 0.00).
